gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-coptic: Azonix is wide-mouthed and built like bent tubing, with capitals barely taller than its lowercase and no flicker of weight. Noto Sans Coptic runs on a plain sans middle zone that stays comfortable page after page.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-cuneiform: Commanding, with a hint of sci-fi swagger. Noto Sans Cuneiform has swollen, bead-like lowercase and an e that opens up, so long paragraphs feel plump and easygoing beneath Azonix's flat, unmodulated lines.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-deseret: Azonix looks bent from one length of tubing. Its wide-mouthed letters stay crisp when shrunk, and Noto Sans Deseret adds a wide-looking, approachable lowercase that gives the pair its friendliness.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-devanagar: Azonix traces every stroke at the width of a single stylus. Shrink it down and its wide letters stay crisp, while Noto Sans Devanagari, a plain sans with a compact skyline, is happier when sized up.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-duployan: Azonix is bent tubing, one gauge throughout, with capitals barely above its lowercase. Make it small and its wide letters hold up, whereas Noto Sans Duployan, a plain sans with oversized counters, would swamp anything it was blown up to.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-elbasan: The heading's o has sides and top equally thick, and that gives Azonix its mechanical, authoritative look. Noto Sans Elbasan, a plain sans with large lowercase and open terminals, does the quieter work of carrying the text.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-elymaic: Azonix writes with one fixed nib width, wide and commanding, and it looks best at larger sizes. Noto Sans Elymaic, a sans-serif with open apertures, is the one to trust for the running text.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Steady pen pressure from first letter to last gives Azonix its authoritative, almost engineered look, while capitals sit barely above lowercase. Noto Sans Ethiopic, a plain sans with a tall, sturdy lowercase, grounds it.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-georgian: Azonix looks bent from a single wire, with wide-mouthed letters and capitals only slightly above lowercase, so it earns its keep when big and brief. Noto Sans Georgian handles the rest.
